stemMd: A tall plant with a dominant tall allele is crossed with a homozygous recessive short plant. Of 200 offspring, 103 are tall and 97 short. Which parental genotype best explains the tall parent's offspring under simple Mendelian inheritance?

options.label: D
options.textMd: A genotype cannot influence this ratio

explanationMd: A heterozygote produces dominant and recessive gametes in equal proportions. Crossing it with a recessive homozygote predicts roughly equal tall and short offspring; sampling variation explains 103 versus 97.

distractorRationale.a: The model requires an allele on each homologous chromosome.
distractorRationale.c: This would make the parent short under the stated model.
distractorRationale.e: This predicts all tall offspring in this cross.
